one_liner: Close is a hosted sales CRM with a broad REST API and a vendor-operated MCP server.

auth.notes: OAuth 2.0 is recommended for user-facing integrations. API keys use HTTP Basic authentication.

access.notes: A 14-day trial is the self-serve path to testing the hosted API; there is no permanent free plan. Publishing an OAuth app for other Close customers requires review. The trial-to-API link is stated most directly by a third-party guide.

api.notes: The public reference covers core CRM data with read and write operations.

mcp.notes: Close documents a usable remote MCP server and recommends OAuth 2.0. The supplied MCP search returned no Close-specific result.

verdict.rationale: A developer can test the documented, broad API through a 14-day trial, but the no-payment path is time-limited. Making an OAuth app available to other Close customers requires review.

evidence.quote: Push leads, contacts, activities, and custom data into Close from your website or other systems via the REST API.

All API requests require authentication. Two methods are supported: API Keys — Best for scripts, internal tools, and server-side integrations. Use HTTP Basic Auth with your API key as the username and an empty password. OAuth 2.0 — Best for user-facing integrations.
OAuth 2.0 — Lets each user authorize your app to act on their behalf. Strongly recommended for user-facing integrations that multiple users will authenticate to.
Test with a free trial account, which runs 14 days and needs no credit card; Close documents no separate sandbox.
API keys can be created and managed in your Close account under Settings → Developer → API Keys.
Close doesn’t have a free plan, but you can try it free for 14 days with no credit card.
Click Make Public and submit for review. We’ll review your app and reply by email.
Close runs one production host, https://api.close.com/api/v1, for every account.
Close uses industry-standard REST conventions with predictable URL structures, standard HTTP methods, and JSON request/response bodies.
They represent a company or organization and can contain contacts, tasks, opportunities, and activities.
Build your integration — Use the API Reference to read and write Close data.
The MCP server URL is https://mcp.close.com/mcp and has ‘HTTP Streamable’ and ‘OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)’ support.
We recommend accessing the MCP server via OAuth 2.0 using a supported MCP client (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc).

Securely connect your AI agents and chatbots (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc) with Close MCP or direct API to manage leads, automate follow-ups, send emails, and track sales activities through natural language.
Test with a free trial account, which runs 14 days and needs no credit card; Close documents no separate sandbox.
If you want other Close customers to authorize it, you’ll need to request to make it public and optionally get listed.

problems: Close’s pricing page describes the trial and API separately, rather than explicitly saying in one sentence that trial accounts receive API credentials. The direct trial-API evidence therefore comes from Apideck.
No login wall prevented reading the relevant developer documentation.
name: Close

verification.note: Docs state two methods: API keys via HTTP Basic Auth (key as username, empty password) and OAuth 2.0, which is explicitly best/strongly recommended for user-facing integrations acting for users.

No free plan; a 14-day no-card trial is the self-serve path, and API keys are created in account settings. The trial-to-API sentence is on a third-party page. Public OAuth apps need review, which is a distribution caveat, not a harder path to credentials.
Public docs describe a REST API with JSON and standard HTTP methods, and read/write of leads, contacts, activities, tasks, opportunities, and custom data. Nothing contradicts breadth broad.

Close's own developer page gives a usable server URL (https://mcp.close.com/mcp) and recommends OAuth clients. No quote calls it beta, pilot, or unlaunched. The MCP-search remark in the notes is not in these quotes.
The Composio toolkit page lists Close for agents via Close MCP or the direct API.
Trial-only credentials plus a documented, non-narrow public REST API is buildable_with_caveats with main_blocker trial_only. OAuth review is an extra distribution constraint, not a different blocker.
